entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: " During investigation, examined complainant, witnesses & account holder, analyses the WhatsApp Chat history & Telegram chat history of victim with alleged profiles, Financial transactions & interaction through different social media, CDR analysis, it seems that accused person Bijan Kumar Panda(36) had hired the activated current account with linked pre-activated SIM from the accused Vivekananda Mallick & Sapan Kumar Dalei (45), which were opened with the help of accused Sunit Kumar Das (37).
Similarly Bhabesh Chandra Kabat had hired the activated current account with linked pre-activated SIM from the accused Kamlesh Patel & Deepak Kumar Patel through Rajesh Kumar Behera.

All accounts were collected by accused Anil Hembram from Bijan Kumar Panda(36) & Bhabesh Chandra Kabat and Anil Hembram transferred the same to different locations, like Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, Hyderabad, Kolkata through Courier & Bus.
In return accused Anit Hembram had got Rs. 55,000/- to Rs. 1,00,000/- per account from the fraudsters.
One of them is Prthapani Ranadheer, who is yet to be arrested.
All the alleged accounts has been used for the purpose of transfer of cheated amount by impersonation.
All the fraudulent activities were made through virtual world and operated from different locations......"
8. Copy of the charge sheet submitted by the learned counsel for the Petitioner is taken on record.

9. Considering the role ascribed to the Petitioner and as he is not an employee of the Bank in question and keeping in view that he is the first offender, this Court directs his release on bail on such terms to be fixed by the Court in seisin.
10. Before releasing, learned Court in seisin is requested to verify the criminal antecedent of the Petitioner.
If it comes to fore that the Petitioner has any criminal antecedent, this order shall stand recalled.

11. Additionally, it is directed that the Petitioner shall appear before the jurisdictional police station once every month on such date and time to be fixed by the learned Court in seisin till conclusion of trial.
Certification of such appearance shall be submitted to the Court in seisin.

12. Since the investigation has been kept open, the Petitioner shall not leave the territorial jurisdiction of the learned Court in seisin without its express permission and without intimation to the I.O.
13.
Accordingly, the BLAPL stands disposed of.
14. Urgent certified copy of this order be granted as per rule.
(V  Ayesha  Sapan Kumar Dalei vs State Of Odisha & Another ....
